steps.output:
My top pick is the **Easton 2010 Monarch Mine Vineyard Sauvignon Blanc, Sierra Foothills (92 pts, $18) [3]**. It's the closest to the Sancerre style you're after: crisp, dry and steely, with enough acidity to stand up to the vinaigrette and cut through the creamy goat cheese. Its fennel and citrus notes work well against the earthy sweetness of the beets, and the review itself names a creamy goat cheese salad as a match.

For a second bottle, try the **Leah Jørgensen Cellars 2014 Panner-Hanson Vineyard "Loiregon" Sauvignon Blanc, Rogue Valley (92 pts, $20) [1]**. It's a Loire-inspired Oregon wine with bright acidity and low alcohol, so it stays light enough for the dish. The lime cuts the tang of the chèvre, and the honeydew and sweet hay notes go well with the roasted beets. The reviewer calls anything with goat cheese "sure-fire."

flavor_link.reason: Sauvignon Blanc with goat cheese is a classic bridge. The fennel and citrus in [3] and the honeydew and sweet hay in [1] work against the earthy sweetness of the beets.

Calling [1] 'Loire-inspired' is a fair reading of the 'Loiregon' name.
